title: Business-logic quirks: follow_up string 'false' coerces to true; mark-sent re-stamps and has no state guard; empty PATCH returns 200 no-op
description: Source-verified all three quirks, but REJECTED as a security finding. 7-Question Gate fails Q1/Q4/Q6: every /api/* route requires the shared BOARD_TOKEN (authed(), lines 64-68; enforced lines 346-349, 401 without it), so only the key holder — the board owner — can trigger any of them, on their own board data only. There is no cross-user, privilege-escalation, unauthenticated, or other-user impact; the effect is owner-only data/semantics confusion. Correct home is NOT a security finding and NOT a single bundled security candidate: split into three separate functional bugs for the replica-test bug list (S3/S4). (1) follow_up coercion — functional input-validation bug (S3): validatePatch line 127 does `out.follow_up = !!body.follow_up` with no typeof-boolean check, unlike title/description/column/agent/priority which are strictly validated; the string 'false' (and any non-empty string, 1, {}, []) is truthy and stores true. The same validatePatch is shared by POST create (line 363), so create is affected too; the UI sends a real checkbox boolean so the normal UI path is unaffected. (2) mark-sent re-stamp — functional idempotency/audit bug (S3/S4): lines 414-422 unconditionally set `sent_to_qwenpaw_at = now` and `updated_at = now` with no already-sent check and no done/wont-do guard; re-marking overwrites the original sent timestamp (audit history lost). Note the session value is deterministic (`board-<id8>`, line 417) so only the timestamp changes, and the UI hides the button once sent (line ~307), so the API guard is the missing layer. (3) Empty PATCH — functional validation bug (S4): lines 427-433, `{}` passes validatePatch as `{value:{}}`, then `Object.assign(ticket, {}, {updated_at: now})` bumps updated_at, saves to KV, and returns 200 with no field changed; the same applies to a PATCH containing only unknown fields, which are silently ignored. No live test was run (no board key; do not guess/brute-force it), but live testing would only re-prove these owner-only functional behaviours, not convert them into a security finding.
claimed_root_cause: validatePatch coerces non-boolean follow_up values with !! (the string 'false' becomes true), mark-sent unconditionally re-stamps sent_to_qwenpaw_at with no already-sent guard, and an empty PATCH returns 200 while only bumping updated_at.

title: Corrupt KV value silently returns an empty board; the next write then overwrites (destroys) the stored data
description: The code pattern is real in isolation — loadTickets() at lines 71-80 returns [] on JSON parse failure or a non-array object without .tickets, and POST /api/tickets then load-push-saves that [] plus one new ticket, overwriting the corrupt KV value. A local mock-KV simulation of the verbatim functions confirmed this: corrupt fixture loaded as [], wrong-shape {"foo":1} loaded as [], and a POST-style load+push+save left KV as {"tickets":[new ticket]} with the original ticket gone. But as a finding it fails the 7-Question Gate and is rejected: there is no realistic trigger and no attacker path. The sole writer in the repo is saveTickets() (line 83), which always writes JSON.stringify({tickets, updated_at}) — valid JSON — and there is no other TICKETS.put in the codebase; a KV put is a single atomic write, so a partial write is not a realistic trigger. Corruption would require an already-broken state: a manual operator edit via the Cloudflare dashboard/wrangler kv:put, or another writer sharing the namespace — neither evidenced. An attacker cannot create that state through the API (all /api/* writes go through saveTickets and produce valid JSON), and triggering the overwrite requires the privileged BOARD_TOKEN, so Q1 and Q4 fail. Only POST /api/tickets is destructive after corruption; PATCH/DELETE/comments/mark-sent first do findIndex on the [] load, get -1, and return 404 before any save. Q6 also fails: no live proof (correctly not attempted against live KV) and the board is currently EMPTY per the build report, so there is no data at risk today — a corrupt empty board is indistinguishable from an empty board and a create would destroy nothing. This is at most a defensive-coding / reliability hardening note, not a security finding or a reportable reliability bug. Remediation assessed as correct in direction but optional: fail-closed (loadTickets should throw/return a sentinel, handlers return a distinct 500, and POST must refuse to save) plus a backup KV key written only on successful loads/saves (never backing up a corrupt value) would fix it, but it is hardening, not a required fix.
claimed_root_cause: loadTickets() returns [] on JSON parse failure or wrong-shape KV values, and the next POST create then overwrites the stored value, destroying the prior data.

title: KV race condition: concurrent ticket/comment mutations silently lose data (last-writer-wins on single-key store)
description: Mechanism verified in source and REAL as a reliability defect, but NOT a security finding. Every mutation is load-modify-write on one KV key: loadTickets (line 71-72, KV GET 'tickets') -> mutate in memory -> saveTickets (line 82-83, unconditional KV PUT of the whole board). No version, ETag/If-Match, CAS, lock, or transaction exists anywhere; the board-level updated_at written at line 83 is write-only metadata, never read or compared. Cloudflare KV eventual consistency (noted in the file header, lines 26-28) makes the mechanism worse than a pure overlap race: a stale GET can lose data even for nominally sequential mutations from different edges. However it fails the 7-Question Gate as a security finding: Q1/Q4 — only a BOARD_TOKEN holder can trigger it (authed(), lines 64-68, single shared key, 401 otherwise), and a key holder can already delete/overwrite the entire board via legitimate DELETE/PATCH, so the race gives an attacker nothing they do not already have; Q6 — no live concurrent test was run and none can be run without the key, so impact is 'technically possible' only. The only realistic trigger is the same trusted user in two tabs or a double-click. That is silent self-data-loss on a single-user board: a reliability/correctness bug, not a security boundary violation, privilege escalation, or cross-user impact.
claimed_root_cause: Every mutation is load-modify-write on a single KV key with no version, ETag, CAS, lock, or transaction, so concurrent mutations silently lose data (last-writer-wins), amplified by KV eventual consistency.

title: Location rewrite only covers absolute ORIGIN URLs; protocol-relative or foreign-absolute Location from origin would pass through unrewritten
description: The code gap is real but has no producer: rewriteHeaders in pages/public/_worker.js only rewrites a Location starting with ORIGIN, so a //evil.com or https://evil.com Location from the origin would pass through verbatim. However, exhaustive source inspection of the deployed QwenPaw v2.3.0 (agentscope/qwenpaw:v2.3.0, inside container qwenpaw at /app/src/qwenpaw) finds zero code that can emit a Location header at all — no RedirectResponse, no redirect() call, no Location header set anywhere — and live probes of unauthenticated Pages paths return no Location header. No request, authenticated or not, can produce the claimed foreign redirect, so Q1 of the 7-Question Gate fails and the finding is an unexploitable latent gap, not a vulnerability. The proposed remediation (rewrite/drop any absolute or protocol-relative Location) is still correct, minimal defense-in-depth and would break nothing: the only redirects the origin could ever legitimately emit are same-host absolute ones (e.g. Starlette trailing-slash redirects), which the fix would rewrite to the Pages origin, and no legitimate foreign Location exists.
claimed_root_cause: rewriteHeaders only rewrites a Location starting with ORIGIN, so a protocol-relative or foreign-absolute Location from the origin would pass through unrewritten.

title: Indirect prompt injection via agent-read content is unguarded (skill scanner covers skills only, warn mode)
description: Code trace verified as stated, but the finding fails the 7-Question Gate on multiple questions and is rejected as a standalone vulnerability. Verified facts: skill_scanner mode is 'warn' (config.json:1072; default warn in config.py) so scan findings do not block skills; sandbox_enabled is false (config.json:1076; default false); scan_skill (scanner.py:148) scans skill directories only; cron JobRuntimeSpec.tool_safety defaults to False (models.py:172) and executor.py:200 maps that to ToolExecutionLevel.OFF (all tools without approval). (2) No attacker and no exploit path was identified: in this single-user personal agent, reading email/web/files and acting on them at the owner's direction is the intended behaviour; no copy-pasteable unauthenticated request exists (Q1 fails). (3) The cron OFF-execution arm is unreachable by anyone but the authenticated owner — GET /api/cron/jobs returns 401 unauthenticated on both the Pages proxy and the direct InstaBox URL, and only the owner can create a cron job (Q4 fails). title: Bearer token accepted via ?token= query parameter on every API request
description: Code-confirmed primitive: AuthMiddleware._extract_token in /app/src/qwenpaw/app/auth.py accepts the bearer token from the ?token= query parameter on every request, not only WebSocket upgrades — line 856 unconditionally returns the query token, making the upgrade branch at lines 853-855 dead code. title: Unauthenticated POST /trigger on qwenpaw-routines queues stored prompts, forces origin wake probes, and writes never-expiring KV keys
description: POST /trigger on qwenpaw-routines has no authentication check, unlike POST /api/routines in the same file. Any unauthenticated caller can queue a prompt (up to 2000 chars) as a pending KV entry, force a probe GET to the public QwenPaw URL (waking the InstaBox Free machine), and pollute history. The pending KV put has no expirationTtl and there is no cleanup/pruning code anywhere in the file, so keys accumulate indefinitely. The only throttle is a single global KV timestamp allowing 1 trigger/minute shared by all callers. The stored prompt is not executed in QwenPaw (pending only, by design) and is HTML-escaped when rendered, so no stored-XSS or code execution was demonstrated.
root_cause: POST /trigger has no authentication check, unlike POST /api/routines in the same file; any unauthenticated caller can queue a prompt (up to 2000 chars) as a pending KV entry and force a probe GET to the public QwenPaw URL, and the pending KV put has no expirationTtl and no cleanup/pruning code anywhere in the file.
intended_behavior: Only callers presenting ROUTINE_WEBHOOK_TOKEN can trigger a routine; pending entries expire (for example after 7 days) and stale pending keys are pruned so junk cannot accumulate.

title: Routines /trigger 1/min rate limit is a non-atomic check-then-set and may be bypassable with parallel requests
description: Mechanism verified from source and local simulation, but rejected as a standalone record: the check-then-set is real (L209 get, L211 60s check, L214 probe await widening the window, L223 put; no lock/CAS/transaction anywhere in the file, and KV has no atomic CAS), and a local simulation of that exact interleaving returns [202,202] for two parallel triggers vs [202,429] sequentially. Token-gating /trigger (the fix for the confirmed unauthenticated-trigger finding) makes the race moot for attackers. Fold this as a note under that confirmed finding, not a separate record.
